description: Explain an HTTP status code. Send code, a number from 100 to 599, and optionally method (GET, POST ...). Get back the official name, its class (1xx to 5xx), what it means, which RFC and section define it, whether to retry and how (follow the Location, fix the request first, wait and resend, or never), whether a cache may reuse it by default, and the headers to look at. Covers every code in the IANA HTTP Status Code Registry; unassigned codes are reported as such and treated like the x00 code of their class, as RFC 9110 says. Answer fields: ok, verdict, result, rule, does_not, sources, observation, signature, verify. Errors: ok false with the reason (bad input, too large, hourly limit). Free. No model, no network, nothing you send is stored by the tool, and every answer is signed with LLPRO's key (check it at https://llpro.ai/http-status-explain). Not legal, tax or financial advice.

code.description: The three-digit HTTP status code, 100 to 599.

method.description: Optional: the request method that got this status, to tailor the retry advice (RFC 9110 9.2.2: PUT, DELETE and the safe methods are idempotent).
